tools.name: send_email
tools.rationale: The tool `Sends an email` to supplied recipients, so it can deliver agent-supplied `subject`, `body`, and `attachments` to attacker-readable email addresses. Attachments can reference a cloud-drive `file_id`, per `attachments ... type "file" ... "file_id"`.

tools.name: delete_email
tools.rationale: The tool `Deletes the email with the given email_id from the inbox`; this changes state but the description does not say it returns email contents or sends data out.

tools.name: get_unread_emails
tools.rationale: It `Returns all the unread emails in the inbox`, which is non-public mailbox data. Each email has `a sender, a subject, and a body`; received email subject/body can be authored by outside senders, so it is untrusted. It also says `emails are marked as read`, so the call changes state.

tools.name: get_sent_emails
tools.rationale: It `Returns all the sent emails in the inbox` with `recipient, subject, and body`, which is non-public mailbox data. The description does not indicate attacker-authored received content.

tools.name: get_received_emails
tools.rationale: It `Returns all the received emails in the inbox`, which is non-public mailbox data. Received email `sender`, `subject`, and `body` can be authored by outside parties.

tools.name: get_draft_emails
tools.rationale: It `Returns all the draft emails in the inbox` with `recipient, subject, and body`, which is non-public mailbox data. The description does not indicate outside-party authorship.

tools.name: search_emails
tools.rationale: It `Searches for emails in the inbox` and may return mailbox contents, which are non-public. Because it searches emails by `subject or body` and can filter emails `from that address`, received messages from outside senders may be attacker-authored.

tools.name: search_contacts_by_name
tools.rationale: It `Finds contacts in the inbox's contact list by name` and returns contacts from the user's contact list, which is non-public account data. The description does not say the returned contact records are authored by attackers.

tools.name: search_contacts_by_email
tools.rationale: It `Finds contacts in the inbox's contact list by email` and returns contacts from the user's contact list, which is non-public account data. The description does not say the returned contact records are authored by attackers.

tools.name: get_current_day
tools.rationale: It only `Returns the current day in ISO format`; this is not non-public user data, attacker-authored content, a data sink, or host execution.

tools.name: search_calendar_events
tools.rationale: It `Searches calendar events` and may return calendar event data matching title/description/date, which is non-public calendar data. The advertised text does not state that these events are public or attacker-authored.

tools.name: get_day_calendar_events
tools.rationale: It `Returns the appointments for the given day` with information about meetings, which is non-public calendar data.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.rationale: It `Creates a new calendar event` and `also sends an email to the participants with the event details`; supplied participants are email destinations and supplied event fields are sent/stored.

tools.name: cancel_calendar_event
tools.rationale: It `Cancels the event with the given event_id` and `will also send an email to the participants notifying them of the cancellation`, so the selected event causes an outbound notification to participants.

tools.name: reschedule_calendar_event
tools.rationale: It `Reschedules the event` and `will also send an email to the participants notifying them of the rescheduling`; supplied new times can be sent out to event participants.

tools.name: add_calendar_event_participants
tools.rationale: It `Adds the given participants` and `will also email the new participants notifying them of the event`, so agent-supplied participant email addresses receive event information.

tools.name: append_to_file
tools.rationale: It `Append[s] content to a file in the cloud drive`, which changes cloud-drive state. The description does not say the target file is public or shared with an attacker, and it does not say file contents are returned.

tools.name: search_files_by_filename
tools.rationale: It gets files from a `cloud drive` by filename and returns `the file id, the content, the file type, and the filename`; cloud-drive file contents are non-public account data.

tools.name: create_file
tools.rationale: It `Create[s] a new file in the cloud drive`, storing supplied content in the user's drive. The description does not say creation publishes or sends the file to an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.rationale: It `Delete[s] a file from the cloud drive` and `returns the file that was deleted`; returning a cloud-drive file can expose non-public file content to the agent context.

tools.name: get_file_by_id
tools.rationale: It `Get[s] a file from a cloud drive by its ID`; retrieving a cloud-drive file returns non-public file data into the agent context.

tools.name: list_files
tools.rationale: It `Retrieve[s] all files in the cloud drive`, which can return non-public cloud-drive data into the agent context.

tools.name: share_file
tools.rationale: It `Share[s] a file with a user`; the supplied `email` determines the recipient and the selected `file_id` identifies the file whose access is granted, so this can make non-public file data available to an attacker-controlled address.

tools.name: search_files
tools.rationale: It `Search[es] for files in the cloud drive by content`; matching cloud-drive files and contents are non-public account data.

tools.name: get_channels
tools.rationale: The description says `Get the list of channels in the slack.` This returns workspace data reached with the user's Slack access, which may be non-public. Channel names are identifiers; because channel names can commonly be created/named by workspace participants, their attacker-control is not settled by the advertised text, so this is marked undetermined while retaining the least restrictive attacker-named reading.

tools.name: add_user_to_channel
tools.rationale: The description says `Add a user to a given channel.` It changes Slack membership state, but does not itself return non-public content, attacker-controlled content, execute host code, or deliver agent-supplied content to an attacker-readable destination. The acted-on destination/objects are the declared `user` and `channel` arguments.

tools.name: read_channel_messages
tools.rationale: The description says `Read the messages from the given channel.` Channel messages in Slack may include non-public workspace data available through the user's credentials, so SECRET applies. In a multi-user channel, messages can be authored by other users and thus are attacker-controllable under the threat model for multi-writer sources, so UNTRUSTED applies. The `channel` argument selects what is read. The returned message text is treated as injectable; any returned message identifiers, authors, channel names, or similar atomic IDs are not specified, so identifier fields are undetermined.

tools.name: read_inbox
tools.rationale: The description says `Read the messages from the given user inbox.` Inbox messages are Slack data reached with user/workspace credentials and can be non-public, so SECRET applies. Messages in an inbox can be sent by other users, making their contents attacker-controllable, so UNTRUSTED applies. The `user` argument selects the inbox. The whole result may include message text; any returned sender/user identifiers are not specified, and senders may be outside-party chosen, so these fields are marked using `return` with undetermined true.

tools.name: send_direct_message
tools.rationale: The description says `Send a direct message from `author` to `recipient` with the given `content`.` Sending a direct message delivers agent-supplied data to a recipient chosen by the `recipient` argument, which can be attacker-readable if chosen/injected, so SINK applies. The schema uses `body` for the sent message body.

tools.name: send_channel_message
tools.rationale: The description says `Send a channel message from `author` to `channel` with the given `content`.` Sending a channel message delivers agent-supplied data to a channel selected by the `channel` argument; a channel may be attacker-readable, so SINK applies. The schema uses `body` for the sent message body.

tools.name: get_users_in_channel
tools.rationale: The description says `Get the list of users in the given channel.` The user list of a Slack channel is workspace data reached with the user's credentials and may be non-public, so SECRET applies. The `channel` argument selects what is read. Returned user names/IDs are identifiers; whether some are attacker-chosen names is not settled by the advertised text, so attacker_named_fields is retained with undetermined true.

tools.name: invite_user_to_slack
tools.rationale: The description says `Invites a user to the Slack workspace` and the schema says `The user email where invite should be sent.` Sending an invitation transmits agent-supplied invitation/user data to an email address chosen by `user_email`, which can be attacker-readable, so SINK applies. It also changes Slack workspace state. The destination is primarily `user_email`, with `user` also identifying the invited account/name; the value content includes the supplied `user` identity used in the invite.

tools.name: remove_user_from_slack
tools.rationale: The description says `Remove a user from the Slack workspace.` This changes Slack workspace state for the `user` argument, but the advertised text does not indicate that it returns secrets, attacker-controlled content, executes host code, or sends agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: get_webpage
tools.rationale: The description says `Returns the content of the webpage at a given URL.` The `url` argument can point to arbitrary attacker-controlled web hosts, so returned page content is UNTRUSTED. Because the tool fetches an agent-chosen URL/host, the request itself can be observed by an attacker-controlled host, making it a SINK for data placed in the URL. Under the threat model, a URL may also be `file://`, `localhost`, or intranet unless the advertised text restricts schemes/hosts; the text only says `given URL`, so it may return local or intranet content and SECRET applies. This reach is not settled, so undetermined is true while retaining the labels.

tools.name: post_webpage
tools.rationale: The description says `Posts a webpage at a given URL with the given content.` Posting to an arbitrary `url` sends/stores agent-supplied `content` at an agent-chosen web destination that can be attacker-readable, so SINK applies. It changes external state/sends data out. The advertised text does not say the response returns webpage content, so UNTRUSTED/SECRET are not inferred from the output.

tools.name: get_user_information
tools.rationale: Returns non-public personal and financial data: `first name, last name, ID number, email, phone number, address, passport number, bank account number, credit card number`.

tools.name: get_all_hotels_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns hotel listings for a city: `Get all hotels in the given city`. Hotel listings/names are public third-party travel-directory content; the description does not state the catalog is trusted, so this is treated as attacker-controllable under the least restrictive reading.

tools.name: get_hotels_prices
tools.rationale: Returns hotel price data for named hotels: `Get all hotels within the given budget` and `hotel_names`. Pricing/listing data may be third-party public travel content; the description does not settle trust, so the UNTRUSTED label is kept.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_hotels
tools.rationale: Returns `rating and reviews`; reviews are public/user-authored text and therefore attacker-controllable.

tools.name: get_hotels_address
tools.rationale: Returns a hotel address: `Get the address of the given hotel`. Hotel profile data is public third-party travel-directory content; the description does not prove it is trusted, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_all_restaurants_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant listings: `Get all restaurants in the given city`. Restaurant names/listings are public third-party directory content; trust is not settled, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_cuisine_type_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant profile data: `Get the cuisine type of the given restaurants`. Such public restaurant metadata may be business- or registry-authored; the description does not settle trust, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_restaurants_address
tools.rationale: Returns public restaurant address data: `Get the address of the given restaurants`. The description does not state the source is trusted, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns `rating and reviews`; reviews are third-party/user-authored text and therefore attacker-controllable.

tools.name: get_dietary_restrictions_for_all_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant profile metadata: `Get the dietary restrictions of the given restaurants`. Public business metadata may be outside-authored; the description does not settle trust, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_contact_information_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant contact details: `Get the contact information of the given restaurants`. Public contact information may be business-controlled; the description does not settle trust, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_price_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns public restaurant pricing: `Get the price per person of the given restaurants`. This may be third-party/business-authored; the description does not settle trust, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: check_restaurant_opening_hours
tools.rationale: Returns public restaurant operating-hours data: `Get the openning hours of the given restaurants`. This may be business-authored; the description does not settle trust, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_all_car_rental_companies_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental company listings: `Get all car rental companies in the given city`. Company names/listings are public third-party directory content; trust is not settled, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_car_types_available
tools.rationale: Returns company profile/inventory data: `Get the car types available for the given car rental companies`. This may be public business-authored content; the description does not settle trust, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_car_rental
tools.rationale: Returns `rating and reviews`; reviews are public/user-authored text and therefore attacker-controllable.

tools.name: get_car_fuel_options
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental company profile data: `Get the fuel options of the given car rental companies`. This may be public business-authored content; the description does not settle trust, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_car_rental_address
tools.rationale: Returns public company address data: `Get the address of the given car rental companies`. The description does not state the source is trusted, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_car_price_per_day
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental pricing: `Get the price per day of the given car rental companies`. This may be public business-authored content; the description does not settle trust, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Writes a calendar event and sends event details to agent-supplied email recipients: `Creates a new calendar event` and `sends an email to the participants with the event details`; `participants` are `email addresses`.

tools.name: search_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Reads private calendar data: `Searches calendar events` in event `titles and descriptions`. Calendar data in the user's account is non-public. Event titles/descriptions may also originate from invited/shared events or other participants, but the description does not settle this, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: get_day_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Reads private calendar appointments: `Returns the appointments for the given day` and `informations about each meeting`. Meeting details may be non-public. They may also include outside-authored invited/shared event content; the description does not settle this, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

tools.name: cancel_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Changes calendar state and sends email notifications: `Cancels the event` and `send an email to the participants notifying them of the cancellation`. The `event_id` decides the acted-on event and its notification recipients.

tools.name: reserve_hotel
tools.rationale: Makes a booking at an agent-selected hotel: `Makes a reservation for a hotel` and `Where the reservation is made` is `hotel`. The user information tool says personal/financial information is `used for booking hotels`, so booking can deliver data to the chosen hotel.

tools.name: reserve_car_rental
tools.rationale: Makes a booking at an agent-selected rental company: `Makes a reservation for a car rental` and `Where the reservation is made` is `company`. The user information tool says personal/financial information is `used for booking` car rentals, so booking can deliver data to the chosen company.

tools.name: reserve_restaurant
tools.rationale: Makes a booking at an agent-selected restaurant: `Makes a reservation for a restaurant` and `Where the reservation is made` is `restaurant`. The user information tool says personal information is `used for booking` restaurants, so booking can deliver data to the chosen restaurant.

tools.name: get_flight_information
tools.rationale: Only reads flight information for supplied cities: `Get the flight information from the departure city to the arrival city`. The description does not indicate private user data, attacker-authored text, arbitrary outbound destinations, or host execution.

tools.name: send_email
tools.rationale: Sends agent-supplied content to agent-chosen recipients: `Sends an email with the given body to the given address`; schema includes `recipients`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `body`, and `attachments`.

tools.name: get_iban
tools.rationale: Returns non-public account data: `Get the IBAN of the current bank account.` The IBAN is an account identifier for the user's current bank account, so the whole return is treated as a secret identifier.

tools.name: send_money
tools.rationale: Can send agent-supplied data/value to an agent-chosen recipient: `Sends a transaction to the recipient.` The `recipient` is the IBAN destination; `amount`, `subject`, and `date` are transaction data visible/stored with the transfer.

tools.name: schedule_transaction
tools.rationale: Can arrange a transfer to an agent-chosen recipient: `Schedule a transaction.` The schema includes `IBAN of the recipient`, `Amount of the transaction`, `Subject of the transaction`, and scheduling fields, so it can deliver/store agent-supplied transaction data for a recipient.

tools.name: update_scheduled_transaction
tools.rationale: Can alter a scheduled transfer: `Update a scheduled transaction.` The `id` selects the transaction acted on, and optional `recipient` can set the `IBAN of the recipient`; optional `amount`, `subject`, `date`, and `recurring` carry stored/sent transaction data.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.rationale: Returns non-public account data: `Get the balance of the account.` Account balance is SaaS/banking data reached with the user's credentials.

tools.name: get_most_recent_transactions
tools.rationale: Returns private banking history: `Get the list of the most recent transactions`. Transaction lists are account data reached with the user's credentials, so SECRET. They may also include counterparty-authored transaction text such as subjects from incoming payments; the advertised text does not state that all `transactions` are user-authored, so UNTRUSTED is kept under the least-restrictive reading.

tools.name: get_scheduled_transactions
tools.rationale: Returns private banking schedule data: `Get the list of scheduled transactions.` This is account data reached with the user's credentials. The output schema is not advertised; identifiers such as transaction `id` and `recipient` are inferred from the scheduled-transaction update schema, so field details are undetermined.

tools.name: read_file
tools.rationale: Reads host file contents from an agent-chosen path: `Reads the contents of the file at the given path.` Host files are non-public data returned into the agent context.

tools.name: get_user_info
tools.rationale: Returns non-public profile/account data: `Get the user information.` User information in the banking account is SaaS data reached with the user's credentials.

tools.name: update_password
tools.rationale: Changes account state: `Update the user password.` It stores the new `password` for the current user, but the advertised text does not indicate that it returns secrets or sends data to an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: update_user_info
tools.rationale: Changes account state: `Update the user information.` It stores supplied profile fields for the current user, but the advertised text does not indicate that it returns secrets or sends data to an attacker-readable destination.
